rows.title: Improve experience when using Codespaces
Allow to view multiple items the history in embedded browser
Address suggestions on using address bar.
Responsive Layouts - Like Devices (sm, md, lg, xl) & Viewport dimensions
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed examples and prototype. This capability is still useful, but Live Preview now opens embedded previews in VS Code's Integrated Browser by default through `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser`; responsive presets, device emulation, and viewport dimensions are therefore primarily browser-toolbar functionality rather than server functionality. This remains the oldest canonical request, and the narrower https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/494 overlaps with it. We should keep this open while determining the appropriate Integrated Browser support rather than add separate controls to Live Preview's legacy bundled browser.

rows.title: Firefox support
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. Firefox is now available for regular external previews through `livePreview.customExternalBrowser`, while using that selection for a debug preview is still tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/422. Since completing that issue would cover Firefox DevTools/debug support requested here, consolidating this as a duplicate.
rows.verifyEvidence: A asks for Firefox debugging/devtools support generally; B is a narrower bug that debug preview ignores the customExternalBrowser setting, which wouldn't deliver Firefox debug-adapter support.

rows.title: Changing the port breaks reloading
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The WebSocket using port 81 when the preview is on port 80 is intentional: Live Preview currently runs separate HTTP and WebSocket servers, with the reload socket normally using the next port. The failure is still valid, though—the server should either select a working WebSocket port or clearly report why live reload could not start instead of failing silently. The occupied-port handling in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/262 is related, but this report should remain open until the startup and error-reporting path is handled reliably.

rows.title: Feature request: Add option to provide a wrapper html page (with additional css or js files included)
New feature request: select element
Support auto lock groups
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This is now supported by VS Code core: Live Preview is listed in `workbench.editor.autoLockGroups` and is enabled there by default. The implementation landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c2ed45b371d4c0d9363b6c5f4b75ccd3cb3c6e8b, so this can be closed as completed.
rows.verifyEvidence: Diff registers 'mainThreadWebview-browserPreview' labeled Live Preview in AUTO_LOCK_EXTRA_EDITORS and default-enabled set, making it selectable in workbench.editor.autoLockGroups exactly as requested.

rows.title: Add some of the capabilities from Brackets
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for tracking these Brackets-style workflows. Live element highlighting is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/149, and follow-along scrolling is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/214. Those issues do not cover the whole request here, particularly live CSS updates and navigating from a previewed element to its source. Since Live Preview now uses VS Code's Integrated Browser by default, the browser/editor interaction pieces also need a maintainer decision about what belongs in this extension versus microsoft/vscode, so this umbrella should remain open until the remaining capabilities are clarified or extracted.

rows.title: Live Preview "Host IP" setting does not support IPv6 addresses
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed proposal and follow-up testing. This remains a real feature gap on current `main`: `ConnectionManager` still validates with `net.isIPv4`, and several HTTP and WebSocket addresses are assembled from the host directly, so IPv6 support requires both accepting the address and formatting IPv6 URL authorities correctly. The earlier change was reverted in 0.2.11 after the retest exposed that broader work, and I could not find another open issue or PR that now owns it, so this should remain open.

rows.title: Video not loading in Safari due to missing byte-range support
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is still present on current `main`: the server advertises `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, but it does not inspect the request's `Range` header and always returns the complete file with status 200. Supporting Safari video playback here requires real partial-response handling (`206`, `Content-Range`, the selected `Content-Length`, and a bounded file stream), so this remains a valid server-side bug.

rows.title: Make Live Preview work on the web
Add ignore file for injected script
Project breaks on unplanned "update-path" messages
Follow along scroll?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. Live Preview does not currently have a `livePreview.*` setting for synchronized editor/preview scrolling or bidirectional text selection. This remains the canonical request for follow-along scrolling: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/593 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/642 were closed as duplicates of this issue, while the related element-highlighting work is discussed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/149. Keeping this open in the Backlog for a product and implementation decision, particularly around support through VS Code's default Integrated Browser.

rows.title: watch files settings
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional context. This remains a valid feature request: current Live Preview watches the workspace broadly and does not expose a `livePreview.watchFiles` or equivalent scope setting. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/548 tracks the related request to ignore files that should not cause reloads, but this issue is broader because positive watch patterns are also relevant to generated files and external watch scripts. A future design should handle include and exclude patterns together so it avoids unrelated refreshes without recreating the timing problems of the earlier implementation.

rows.title: PDF in iframe tag causes File Explorer pop-up on refresh
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. Live Preview now uses VS Code's Integrated Browser by default, while the bundled browser involved when this was reported is still available behind `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser: false`. Could you retest the project with current VS Code and Live Preview and let us know what happens with that setting first at `true` and then at `false`? Please also include both version numbers and note whether Windows File Explorer opens in either case. That will show whether this remains specific to the bundled browser or also affects the current default preview.

rows.title: Consider changing default time for server to turn off to be instant
Command for re-opening live preview editor
Not correctly checking if websocket server is occupied before using it
on changes to saved files setting doesn't work outside of workspace
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for verifying this. The change in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/309 added an out-of-workspace save listener, but the failed verification and reopen show that it did not resolve the end-to-end behavior. Current `main` still contains that listener, so this should remain open while we add a focused regression test for saving a loose file with `livePreview.autoRefreshPreview` set to `On Changes to Saved Files` and trace the refresh through the active loose-file server and preview.

rows.title: Switching between single and multi-root will not properly handle panel
Live preview reloads when adding a new workspace root
Live preview task should use the radio tower icon
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This remains blocked on VS Code exposing a supported icon field for extension-contributed tasks. The attempted manifest entry was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/583 because it had no effect, and the linked core API request https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/201011 was later closed for lack of votes rather than implemented. If core gains that capability, Live Preview should use it to assign the radio-tower icon here.

rows.title: Add option to hide the address bar
Allow setting host IP to 0.0.0.0
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional use cases. The direct LAN-address case is working, and the remaining request here is specifically to support `livePreview.hostIP: "0.0.0.0"` so the server can listen on all available interfaces while Live Preview still generates a reachable HTTP/WebSocket address and chooses an available port. The HTTP 401 reports through tunnels appear to be a separate authentication or port-forwarding problem; that scenario is tracked at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/462.

rows.title: Feature request: support viewing of shared Live Share servers in the Live Preview embedded browser
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the feature request. This is still a real gap on current `main`: Live Preview declares `virtualWorkspaces: false`, and its current preview flow assumes it can access workspace files through local filesystem paths and start its own server. The newer `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` setting changes where that locally served URL opens, but it does not let a Live Share guest consume the host's shared-server URL. A suitable implementation would keep the server on the host and add a guest-side path that opens the shared URL through VS Code's Integrated Browser without trying to serve the virtual workspace.

rows.title: Place cursor from preview in editor
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the feature request. This is already tracked by the older, broader request at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/149, which covers selecting an element in the preview and navigating to its HTML source in the editor, along with the reverse synchronization. I would consolidate the right-click-to-source behavior described here into that issue.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the same capability: a devtools-style element picker in the preview that selects/places the cursor at the corresponding HTML source in the editor.

rows.title: Warn users if external browser opens invalid URL
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for recording this. The bundled preview path still passes a scheme-less value such as `google.ca` unchanged to the external-browser helper, and that helper does not await or report whether opening the URI succeeded. The Integrated Browser is now the default, so this mainly affects users with `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` set to `false`, but the underlying fallback-browser issue remains.

rows.title: Server Logging for Non-workspace files
Resource Scope for Default Preview Path
`Live Preview: Show Debug Preview (External Browser)` doesn't respect `livePreview.customExternalBrowser`
Consider respecting server root even if the directory doesn't exist
Show progress while external browser is starting
Allow query parameters in preview path setting
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This is still a real gap on current `main`: both `livePreview.defaultPreviewPath` and `livePreview.start.preview.atFileString` are resolved as filesystem paths, and the query portion is not carried into the URL opened by the embedded, Integrated Browser, or external preview. An address-oriented command, as suggested above, looks like a good way to preserve the existing file-path command contract; the implementation should also merge the Integrated Browser's `vscode-livepreview=true` parameter with the caller's query string.

rows.title: Live preview reloads on editor changes even when not visible
Injected script should be aware of whether it's inside webview or not
401 when using remote tunnel
Persistent status bar item to show when server is off also
[Feature request] Allow setting multiple preferred Server Roots as one string
Support Remote Repositories
[ Question ] What about PHP files preview?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the continued interest. Live Preview currently serves workspace files statically and does not run a PHP interpreter, so `.php` files cannot produce rendered server-side output through its server today. This remains the canonical feature request for deciding whether a constrained PHP or external application-server integration belongs in Live Preview.

rows.title: [Feature Request] Add "Toggle Device Toolbar" to the options
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. The extension-side responsive-preview work is already tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/116, which covers device-size controls, viewport dimensions, and a responsive-mode toggle, so this can be consolidated there. With current default settings, Live Preview opens VS Code's Integrated Browser, whose overflow menu now includes an emulation toolbar for viewport sizes and device presets.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request device/responsive viewport emulation in the embedded preview — A asks for DevTools' Toggle Device Toolbar, B for breakpoint size toggles plus viewport dimensions; the same capability, and A itself cites #116.

rows.title: command 'livePreview.start.preview.atFile' not found
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the reports and the version comparisons. The command is still declared and registered in the current extension, so this message usually means that extension activation failed before registration completed; the command-not-found notification does not include the underlying error. If this still occurs, please share your current Live Preview and VS Code versions, whether this is a local desktop window or a remote session, and the entries from both the `Extension Host` and `Window` channels under `Developer: Show Logs` immediately after clicking Show Preview. Please also include any non-default `livePreview.hostIP` or `livePreview.portNumber` values.

rows.title: Create a launch.json configuration for live preview
"Open Devtools Pane" does not work in browser-based Codespaces
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed cross-browser testing and for explaining why the keyboard shortcut is not sufficient on mobile. Live Preview now uses VS Code's Integrated Browser by default, so could you retest this in a current browser-based Codespace and share your VS Code and Live Preview versions? Please also try once with `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` at its default and once set to `false`, and say whether an "Open Devtools Pane" action is shown in each preview and what happens when it is selected. That will tell us whether the remaining issue is in Live Preview's bundled browser or in VS Code's Integrated Browser.

rows.title: Add custom field for browser path
[Feature request] Auto preview active opened file
Live preview extension doesn't display window at full height in codespaces
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the reproducible project. The current bundled preview CSS sizes the iframe to `height: 100%` without giving its `.content` container a definite height, which is consistent with the Codespaces, Gitpod, and Firefox/code-server reports here. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/751 proposes a direct layout fix and references this issue, so this should remain open while that change is reviewed and validated.

rows.title: External browser can't be found after renaming browser executable
Explain possible Internal (Embedded) vs External Browser version (capabilities) mismatch.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for clarifying the intent. This documentation gap still exists: the README's FAQ currently mentions cache and client-side state, but not that embedded and external previews can use different browser runtimes and therefore support different web-platform features. The wording should now distinguish VS Code's Integrated Browser, the bundled browser used when `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` is disabled, and the user's external browser. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/539 covers the separate naming inconsistency, so this issue should remain open for the capability explanation.

rows.title: Embedded vs Internal Preview documentation inconsistency
Create `ignore` setting for livepreview auto-reloading
Make sure CORP headers are sent
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed Codespaces validation steps. Current `main` still sends `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin`, while the later attempt to add `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` was reverted because it broke iframe, image, and video linking. Since this was reopened after those changes and remains under verification, the next step is an end-to-end retest on a current Codespace with `?vscode-coi=on`, confirming both the response headers and whether the preview loads. This should remain open until that verification establishes whether CORP alone now covers the scenario or additional work is still needed.

rows.title: Stuck on "Opening Server..."
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reports. The useful distinction here is that the server starts and its URL works externally, while the embedded tab does not open. Since these reports, Live Preview 0.4.17 introduced VS Code's Integrated Browser and current releases use it by default. Could someone still seeing this retest with current VS Code and Live Preview 0.4.20, then report whether `Live Preview: Show Preview (Internal Browser)` fails with `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` set first to `true` and then to `false`? Please also include the exact VS Code version and anything added to the Developer Tools console after running the command. That will distinguish a current Integrated Browser problem from the extension's legacy bundled-browser path.

rows.title: Support for SPA
Live Preview does not resolve file when html extension is not provided.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This behavior is not currently supported on `main`: the server checks the requested path exactly and only adds `index.html` when the path is an existing directory. The linked implementation in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/671 is intended to add extensionless HTML resolution, so this issue should remain open while that PR is reviewed and completed.

rows.title: Launch as http://localhost instead of http://127.0.0.1?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional examples and investigation. This remains a valid backlog request: current `main` still restricts `livePreview.hostIP` to IPv4 addresses, and the same host is used for both the HTTP preview URL and live-reload WebSocket URL. Supporting this safely should keep the server bound to the loopback interface while consistently advertising `localhost` for both URLs, so integrations that distinguish the hostname work without losing live reload.

rows.title: Problem with "charset=ISO-8859-1"
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed sample and the curl confirmation. This is still present in the current server code: injectable HTML is read explicitly as UTF-8, passed through the reload-script injector, encoded as UTF-8 again, and served with `charset=UTF-8`. That corrupts ISO-8859-1 bytes before the page or a loaded fragment reaches either browser, so this is not limited to the embedded preview. The server should preserve or correctly transcode the document encoding and send a matching response charset. Until that is fixed, converting the participating HTML files and their charset declarations to UTF-8 is the most reliable workaround.

rows.title: fragment/anchor in Uri is ignored when preview loose file
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the valid-versus-invalid URI comparison. This is still visible in the current source: the preview path is built from `Uri.fsPath`, while the URI's `fragment` is never carried into the resulting preview URL, so `.with({ fragment: 'duration-prop' })` cannot navigate to that anchor. The fix should preserve the fragment for both workspace and loose files across the embedded and external preview targets, with care to keep the Integrated Browser's query parameter before the fragment.

rows.title: !doctype is case-sensitive
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is part of the broader live-reload script placement problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/711. The current injector searches for `!DOCTYPE` case-sensitively, and the implementation proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/746 replaces that search with a case-insensitive HTML-preamble scan. I’m consolidating this report there; its lowercase-doctype example should be retained as a test case.
rows.verifyEvidence: A is case-sensitive matching of a lowercase `<!doctype>`/head marker; B is the injector failing to skip HTML comments containing head-like text — distinct defects in the same naive injection logic.

rows.title: Allow previewing from codeblocks in chat
Incorrect Content-Type header for XHTML files
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and suggested fix. This still appears to be present on current `main`: `ContentLoader.getFileStream` infers the MIME type from the `.xhtml` path, but when the open document has the `html` language ID it injects the reload script and then unconditionally replaces that type with `text/html`. The proposed fix in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/689 was closed without merging, so the XHTML path still needs an implementation and regression test that preserve `application/xhtml+xml` while retaining live reload.

rows.title: Enable Auto-Preview on File Switch
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request and the additional example. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/530, which covers automatically following the active HTML file in Live Preview. The suggestion here to keep the most recently viewed HTML page when switching to related CSS or JavaScript files is useful detail for that same behavior, so the reports can be consolidated there.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both request the same capability: the Live Preview pane should automatically follow and re-render whichever HTML file becomes the active editor tab.

rows.title: customizable date format
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and for offering to contribute. Current main still localizes the generated index headings but formats each modification time with a fixed `M/DD/YY, H:mm:ss` pattern, and there is no existing `livePreview.*` setting for this. A focused change should make the directory-index date locale-aware by default and avoid unintentionally changing the server-task and preview-console timestamps that currently share the same formatter; directory-index test coverage would also be useful.

rows.title: it is not downloading having issue
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you clarify what is continuously buffering: downloading/installing the Live Preview extension, starting the Live Preview server, or loading your page in the preview? Please include the exact steps, what you expected to happen, a screenshot or short recording, and your Live Preview extension version, VS Code version, and operating system. If a preview page is failing to load, please also say whether you are using desktop VS Code or a remote/Codespaces environment, whether `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` is enabled, and paste any errors from the `Embedded Live Preview Console` Output channel or Help > Toggle Developer Tools.

rows.title: Javascript injected in non-html/javascript files
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The current server does classify every file without an extension as injectable, so an extensionless JSON response is modified with the Live Preview script even though its fallback response type is `text/plain`. That confirms this as a server-side correctness issue. The related configuration proposal at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/204 may provide part of the solution, but the default behavior here still needs to distinguish extensionless HTML from non-HTML content without corrupting the response.

rows.title: CSS clip path URL to SVG file not working
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you retest this on the current Live Preview and VS Code versions and share a minimal folder containing the HTML, CSS, and referenced SVG? Please also say whether `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` is enabled, then try it once with that setting enabled and once disabled and report which preview fails. If possible, include any errors from Help > Toggle Developer Tools. That comparison will show whether this is in VS Code's Integrated Browser, the extension's bundled preview, or the served content path.

rows.title: Live preview extension is not working
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you describe the exact steps you take and what happens afterward—for example, whether no preview tab opens, it stays on “Opening Server…”, or it opens an error or blank page? Please retest with current VS Code and Live Preview versions and include a screenshot, your `livePreview.hostIP`, `livePreview.serverRoot`, and `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` settings, plus any output from the `Embedded Live Preview Console` or `Live Preview: Start Server Logging`. If possible, also share a minimal folder that reproduces the problem.

rows.title: Live preview script injected into comment
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the additional analysis. The current `_injectIntoFile` implementation does scan the entire document with a permissive head-tag expression, so both the comment case and the `<header>` case are present on `main`. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/746 is an open fix candidate for this issue; it should remain open while that PR is reviewed and targeted regression tests are added.

rows.title: problem
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you describe exactly what happens when you try to run the website: the steps you take, what you expect to see, and what appears instead? A screenshot would help. Please also include your Live Preview extension version, VS Code version, operating system, whether this is desktop or a remote/Codespaces session, and whether you are using the Live Preview status-bar item and its default port 3000 rather than another live-server extension. If the server starts, please paste any errors from the `Embedded Live Preview Console` Output channel or from `Live Preview: Start Server Logging`.

rows.title: Extension not live reloading - maybe because of arm
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the console output. The embedded preview implementation has changed since this was filed, so could you confirm whether this still happens with the current Live Preview and VS Code versions? Please include your Windows version and the values of `livePreview.autoRefreshPreview` and `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser`. It would also help to check whether the served page reloads when opened with **Live Preview: Show Preview (External Browser)**, and whether changing `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` to `false` changes the result. If it still fails, please share the `Embedded Live Preview Console` output and any WebSocket errors shown in Help > Toggle Developer Tools after editing and saving the file.

rows.title: icon is missing
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you share a screenshot showing where the icon is missing and confirm whether it still happens with the current Live Preview and VS Code versions while an `.html` file is open? If you mean the Show Preview button in the upper-right of the editor, please right-click the editor-title actions or open the `...` menu and check whether `Show Preview` is enabled; also let us know whether `Live Preview: Show Preview (Internal Browser)` appears and works from the Command Palette. That will show whether this is a hidden VS Code action or an extension activation problem.

rows.title: Doesn't work in virtual enviorment
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Could you clarify what you mean by a “virtual environment” here—for example Remote - SSH, WSL, a dev container, Codespaces, Live Share, a virtual workspace, or something else? Please also show what is being disabled, ideally with a screenshot, and list the exact steps that trigger it, your VS Code and Live Preview extension versions, OS, and whether the status bar says `Live Preview` or `Go Live`. If Live Preview is the extension being disabled, please include any message shown on its Extensions page and relevant output from the `Embedded Live Preview Console` or Developer Tools console (Help > Toggle Developer Tools).

rows.title: Not running in Virtual Workspace?
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for asking. A Virtual Workspace is a workspace provided through a virtual filesystem rather than a normal folder available to VS Code's filesystem. Live Preview cannot run there because it needs to start a local server and host the workspace files.

On your Mac, download or clone the project to your computer and open its folder with **File > Open Folder**. You can then preview it normally, or run **Live Preview: Show Debug Preview** from the Command Palette to open an external preview with JavaScript debugging attached.

rows.title: LiveServer Serving Old Version of File Despite Changes
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and for checking with curl and reqwest as well as browsers. The current server code does not keep a persistent file-content cache, but it does serve the in-memory VS Code document when a requested file is open, before reading from disk. Could you retest with the current Live Preview release and share: (1) how the affected files are changed—inside VS Code or by another program—and whether they are open or have unsaved changes, (2) the exact URL and port requested before and after restarting the server, and (3) the output from `Live Preview: Start Server Logging` covering one edit and the following request? A minimal folder containing one affected file and one unaffected file would also help reproduce the difference.

rows.title: Mulitple Previews not working Correctly
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the comparison use case. Live Preview currently reuses one embedded preview: the bundled browser keeps a single panel, and the current Integrated Browser path also asks VS Code to reuse the existing Live Preview tab. There is no `livePreview.*` setting or command that forces a second independent embedded preview, so using separate external-browser tabs is the available workaround today. I suggest keeping this open as the feature request for independently opening multiple previews.

rows.title: Add https server config
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. Live Preview currently always creates a plain HTTP server and does not expose certificate or key settings. Supporting this fully would also require the live-reload WebSocket and generated preview URLs to use the corresponding secure protocols, with clear handling for invalid or untrusted certificates. This should remain open as a feature request for a maintainer scope and security review.

rows.title: Live Preview has stopped working on Mac (used to work before)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report, and thanks for the Windows confirmation. To narrow down where opening the preview stops, please share your current Live Preview extension and VS Code versions, and say exactly which Open Preview button or `Live Preview: ...` command you use. Does the `Live Preview` status-bar item change or does a server URL open successfully in an external browser? Please also include any relevant `livePreview.openPreviewTarget` and `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` settings, plus output from the `Embedded Live Preview Console` channel and any errors shown under Help > Toggle Developer Tools immediately after trying to open the preview. A screenshot or short recording of the button and what happens would also help.

rows.title: images doesn't load when i use live preview in a vite project
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report. This happens because Live Preview is a static file server and does not run Vite's asset-processing or public-directory mapping. The leading slash in `url('/img/png/bg-header.png')` makes Live Preview look for `img/png/bg-header.png` directly under the effective workspace root (or `livePreview.serverRoot`), while Vite's development server resolves the URL according to the Vite project layout.

For a Vite project, the intended setup is to run `npm run dev` and open the Vite URL in VS Code's Integrated Browser. If you want to keep using Live Preview instead, make sure the image exists at that exact path beneath the configured server root, but Vite-specific processing will still not be available.

rows.title: live preview not working
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the reports. That message means the operating system rejected the configured `livePreview.hostIP`; the address must belong to an active network interface on the machine where the Live Preview extension is running. Please share your Live Preview and VS Code versions, OS, whether this is desktop or a Remote/WSL/dev-container/Codespaces session, and the output from `Live Preview: Start Server Logging` after reproducing the problem. Please also confirm that the configured address appears on that machine's active network interface, whether resetting `livePreview.hostIP` to `127.0.0.1` lets the preview open, and whether by the missing button you mean the Live Preview port indicator in the status bar.

rows.title: Automatically switch between tabs.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the confirmations. Live Preview now uses VS Code's Integrated Browser by default, so could you please retest with current Live Preview and VS Code versions and share whether `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` is `true` or `false`? Please also confirm whether the preview tab is VS Code's Integrated Browser or Live Preview's older browser with its own address bar, whether this happens on every edit or only on save, and whether the page or one of its scripts calls `.focus()` after loading. A small HTML file that reproduces it would help distinguish an Integrated Browser issue from the bundled preview's reload behavior.

rows.title: Live Preview omits initial slash of URL pathname if `livePreview.openPreviewTarget` is "External Browser" and `livePreview.serverRoot` ends with a slash.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This still appears to be present on current `main`: when `livePreview.serverRoot` ends with `/`, the relative preview path can be returned as `index.html` instead of `/index.html`, and the external-browser launcher concatenates that directly with the server address. The fix should normalize that relative pathname before constructing the URL and add a regression test for a trailing-slash server root.

rows.title: Preview Server Serves Stale Content from Service Worker Cache
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the confirmation. We have seen this historically when a service worker registered by one preview continued controlling later content on the same host, but the default embedded preview now uses VS Code's Integrated Browser. Could you confirm whether this still happens with current Live Preview and VS Code versions, and include your `livePreview.useIntegratedBrowser` value? The current path encoder leaves `#` unescaped, so the browser treats the remainder of the path as a URL fragment. A focused fix with regression tests is open at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/857; this issue should remain open while that PR is reviewed and verified.

rows.title: File not found.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is a confirmed Windows path-handling bug in Live Preview's generated directory index: the server currently uses the operating system's path separator when constructing a URL, so Windows backslashes are encoded as `%5C` and the links return 404. The open fix at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/856 also identifies this report as the same root cause and adds regression coverage, so this issue should remain open until that PR is resolved.

rows.title: Add CORS setting
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. Live Preview already supports static response headers through `livePreview.httpHeaders`; for example, `"Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*"` allows any origin, while using a specific origin as the value restricts that header accordingly. Could you clarify what remains unsupported in your case—such as an origin allowlist, dynamic origin matching, or OPTIONS preflight requests—and include an example request and the browser error? That will help determine whether a dedicated CORS setting is needed beyond the existing header configuration.

rows.title: Live Preview 401 on remote tunnel with corporate MITM proxy: cert mismatch when host is 127.0.0.1
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed report. Live Preview's local endpoint is plain HTTP (`http://127.0.0.1:3000`); VS Code resolves that through `vscode.env.asExternalUri`, and the tunnel provides the external HTTPS endpoint. That means Live Preview has no local certificate policy to relax, and adding a setting to skip TLS validation would not affect the handshake described here.

Could you capture the response headers and body for the 401, along with the `Live Preview` server-logging task output for the same request? That will show whether the response comes from tunnel ingress or from Live Preview's separate Host/Origin check. The latter is tracked at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/issues/462; a certificate rejection at tunnel ingress would instead belong to VS Code's port-forwarding or tunnel layer.

rows.title: Live Preview generates incorrect directory index URLs using encoded backslashes (%5Cfolder%5Cpath)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and reproduction steps. The current implementation confirms the cause: `createIndexPage` uses the platform-native `path.join` for an href, so Windows backslashes are encoded as `%5C`. The linked fix in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-livepreview/pull/856 switches that URL join to `path.posix.join` while retaining the native join for the actual filesystem path. This issue should remain open until that PR is reviewed and merged.
